notes: Explicit reviewer outcomes for observed SimHub identities that are not curated and are not queued for a guided drive.
A retired identity is a stored pre-rename observation. It is deliberately not aliased onto the renamed record, because it is not selectable in the certified build and cannot be verified there.
These decisions replace hardcoded review outcomes in the manifest generator so the reasoning is reviewable data.
A decision may cite registered source_refs from data/v1/sources.json when an official release establishes the rename.
Third-party content is identified by an irregular name or by an observation that predates the official car's release; the observation date alone is not evidence.
Licensing is a further signal: a manufacturer Reiza does not licence cannot appear as official content.

decisions_list.basis: Maintainer confirmed this identity comes from the FIA-GT1 mod in the ThunderFlash mods pack, not from official AMS2 content. The official Maserati MC12 GT1 is a separate car added in Historical Endurance Pack Pt1 on 2025-10-31, well after this 2024-06-08 observation, and it is curated under its own unprefixed identity. The modded car is not that record and must not be aliased onto it. Not curated and not queued for verification.

Maintainer confirmed AMS2 never shipped a Murcielago R-SV; only unofficial mods provided one, and this identity comes from the FIA-GT1 mod in the ThunderFlash mods pack. It has no successor: the official Murcielago R-GT is a different car added later as Dream Pack Pt2 content on 2025-10-02, not a rename of this identity. Observing it on 2024-12-07, before any official Murcielago existed, is consistent with modded content. Not curated and not queued for verification.

Stored 2024 observation of the pre-rename name. The renamed identity is curated and verified. Not aliased because the old name is not selectable in the certified build.

AMS2 v1.6.9.5 rebranded and replaced the single-make Formula V12 class with Formula Edge, and the release notes identify the former V12 car as Model 1 by warning that old F-V12 liveries need updating for F-Edge Model 1. Deliberately not aliased for two reasons: the name is not selectable in AMS2 1.6.9.91, and the rebrand accompanied rule changes described as the largest downforce drop since 1983, so the retired identity must not inherit the current car's verified controls.

Maintainer confirmed this identity comes from the ThunderFlash mods pack as a mod ported from Project CARS 2, not from official AMS2 content. Its run-together internal name is the only one in the observed inventory that does not follow Reiza's spacing convention, and it was observed on the same day as the pack's FIA-GT1 cars. The official Lamborghini Huracan Super Trofeo EVO2 is a separate car curated under its own properly spaced identity. Not curated and removed from the guided-verification queue.

Maintainer determined this is modded content that is not installed on the verification PC: the car could not be found in AMS2 1.6.9.91 when the guided batch was driven. Reiza does not hold a Mazda licence, so AMS2 ships no official Mazda and no official car can carry this identity. The lowercase 'b' also breaks Reiza's naming convention, which would render the model as 787B. Not curated and removed from the guided-verification queue.

Non-racing safety vehicle. The database answers which physical controls and shifting technique to use for a competition car, so a safety car is outside product scope. It stays unmatched in the client rather than receiving guessed controls.

decisions_list.basis: Stored 2024 observation from before the car was renamed. Loading it in AMS2 1.6.9.91 reports Lotus Renault 98T, in both the high- and low-downforce configurations, so this exact string is no longer produced by the certified build and is not aliased onto the record. Both current identities are carried by ams2.lotus-renault-98t-high-downforce.
